about: Line ceilings the Budgets test enforces. A package ceiling is the package's lines after the reflow to 140 characters and the splits of 2026-10-19, plus twice the lines V3_MILESTONES.md Appendix F still plans for M2 to M7, rounded up to the next hundred (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-19); the corpus keeps its 3,000. A budget counts the physical lines of every file its include globs match, minus its exclude globs and neverCounted. A ceiling rises only with a DECISIONS.md line in the same pull request. planned, plannedFiles and plannedByMilestone are the plan's figures: data to compare against, never a failure.

eachFile.about: Ceilings on each C# file on its own, beside the package budgets (the operator's ruling of 2026-10-19: a package ceiling may rise, the lines per file hold). A file of one of the groups below holds its group's ceiling in physical lines, counted as the package budgets count them, and every line of it holds widthCeiling: its length in characters as a .NET string counts them, a trailing carriage return not counted. A file over its ceiling is split into partial files; a line over the width is broken without changing what it means. These ceilings rise only with a DECISIONS.md line in the same pull request.

code.about: every C# file of the three packages.

tests.about: every C# file of every test project; the corpus under tests/Golden/ is data and has neither ceiling.

code.about: C# in the three packages together; tests are budgeted separately. The ceiling is the sum of the three package ceilings. plannedByMilestone's M3 is Appendix F's re-cut figure, pending the operator's decision on V3_MILESTONES.md section 17 item 20; planned and the M3 rows of plannedFiles are the plan before the re-cut, when M3 planned 4,840.
